heading: Dead letters
notLoaded: Shared Signals is not loaded in this process, so there are no dead-letter queues to report on.
off: Shared Signals is turned off (ssf.enabled), so nothing new is sent or dead-lettered. What is below is held until ssf.deadLetterRetentionS passes.
pushOff: Push delivery is off (ssf.pushDelivery), so no push is made and none can fail. Poll streams have no dead letters.
when.asTable: The same as a table ({busy} of {all} columns hold anything)
when.older: {n} letter(s) are older than the window and are not drawn: the next sweep deletes them. That happens when ssf.deadLetterRetentionS is shortened, and before a process has swept since it started.
why.noAnswer: no HTTP answer — not pushed, or nothing answered
streams.cardTip: This stream's card on Protocols → Shared Signals, where Revive and Drop its dead letters are.
streams.none: Every push stream is delivering and none holds a dead letter.
find.label: Find
find.what: Over the jti, the stream, the reason, the error code, the receiver's status, the event name and type URI and the subject. The counts above are the whole realm's whatever is searched.
letters.none: No dead letters are held in this realm.
process.noSweeps: This process has not swept this realm yet. It sweeps every ssf.deadLetterSweepS.
setting.maxPerStream: letters one stream keeps; past it the oldest go
setting.deadStreamTimeout: seconds of failed pushes before a stream is dead (0: never)
setting.pushConcurrency: pushes in flight per process (0: no cap)
setting.pushBacklog: pushes waiting per process before STS-SSF-0092
setting.pushRetries: retries before a push has failed
intro: Every Security Event Token the transmitter could not deliver and is still holding, in the “{realm}” realm — each realm has dead-letter queues of its own. A letter is kept for ssf.deadLetterRetentionS with the reason, and nothing resends it except the probe that tries to revive a dead stream.
reports.before: This page reports; it changes nothing. Revive a dead stream or drop its letters on that stream's card at
reports.after: — every stream below links to it. Counted {when}.
when.heading: When
when.note: Held letters by when they were dead-lettered, in {bucket} columns over the last {window} — the whole retention window, so a letter that has aged out is gone from the chart as it is from the queue. Point at a column for its counts.
why.heading: Why
why.note: Four causes, each a different thing to do about it. Every other code a failed push can carry is a push that failed, and is broken out below.
streams.heading: Streams
streams.note: Every stream that holds a dead letter or is not delivering. Dead: nothing is pushed to it and one letter is pushed as a probe each ssf.deadStreamTimeoutS. Half-open: failing for that long without being dead, so the next failure kills it. Failing: younger than that. Ever is the stream's own count of every letter it was given, including the ones since deleted.
letters.heading: The letters
letters.note: No token is shown or returned: a SET is a signed statement about somebody. Not signed is a SET for a dead stream, kept as its claims because signing what nothing would receive is the cost dead streams exist to stop.
process.heading: This process
process.warn: Everything in this section is process {pid}'s alone ({role}). In a service with request workers the next refresh may be answered by another process with different numbers, and the push cap is not per realm: every realm's pushes from one process share it, so a burst in one realm can dead-letter another's with STS-SSF-0092.
sweeps.heading: Recent sweeps
sweeps.note: The last twenty sweeps of this realm by this process, newest first. New counts the letters this process added since its previous sweep; held, expired, over cap and orphaned (a letter whose stream is gone) are the shared store as this process found it.
settings.heading: Settings
settings.before: What decides what is dead-lettered and for how long. Changed on
foot.api: the same over the management API
row.noAnswerTip: No HTTP answer: the push was never made, or nothing answered it.
chart.empty: Nothing held was dead-lettered in this window.
chart.label: Dead letters held, by when they were dead-lettered, in {bucket} columns over the last {window}; the busiest column holds {peak}. The same numbers are in the table below.
